caption: The video showcases a white ceramic bowl on a wooden surface, filled with a glossy, viscous red liquid. On the left of the liquid's surface lies a curved, scalloped band of thicker red material arcing from the upper-left toward the lower-center. A bright white specular reflection sits near the bottom of the pool, and a thin lighter-red ring surrounds the main body, separated from the bowl's rim by a pale gap. Over the excerpt this scalloped band slowly recedes leftward and shrinks, its upper portion shortening first until only a thin wavy remnant remains near the left mid-height. The main red liquid, the rim ring, and the reflection spot hold their positions and shapes throughout, while the bowl and background stay fixed in the frame. The visible change is therefore the gradual retraction and diminishing of the scalloped feature, not any translation of the whole scene. No cause or operator is shown to account for the band's motion, and the process appears already underway at the start and still ongoing at the end.

If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
